label: doc_title
text: WORLD OF SPORT.

label: text
text:
CARLISLE AND FOXGLOVE
ENTERTAINED.

label: text
text: It was fortunate indeed that the Carlisle and Foxglove were able to pay us a really decent visit and were not compelled to depart, as usually happens, after only 2 days, says the "B.N. Borneo Herald" Fortunately too the weather, except for a pouring wet and thundery day on the 8th, was excellent throughout, while the Easter holidays which conveniently took place at the same time gave us leisure to entertain our guests and to arrange a good programme of match fixtures, etc.

label: text
text: The following matches were played:

label: text
text:
Sandakan. Sandakan won 2-1.
oth. Soccer. H.M.S. Carlisle vs. Sandakan. Carlisle won 1-0. An even game, the only goal being scored in the last few minutes.

label: text
text: 10th. Soccer. H.M.S. Carlisle vs. H.M.S. Foxglove. Draw, 2-2. A fast game and a very delightful one to watch.

label: text
text:
11th. Golf. Sandakan vs. H. M. Ships. Sandakan won. 5½-2½.
12th. Cricket. Sandakan and H. M. S. Foxglove vs. H. M. S. Carlisle.

label: text
text: First Innings. Carlisle 37. Sanda-kan and Foxglove 68 (Dearle 28). Second Innings. Carlisle 74 for 6 wickets (declared) (Courage 24, Reid 15 not out).

label: text
text: Sandakan and Foxglove, 21 for 4 wickets (stumps drawn 615 p.m.) The collapse of the Carlisle in the first innings was largely due to unsuccessful and over-rash attempts to make short runs, efforts which through the good fielding of the opposing team led to the dismissal of at least three valuable batmen with little or no runs to their credit. The Carlisle team also felded well, especially Surgeon Commander O'Flynn, R.N., who made two extremely fine catches.

label: text
text: 13th, Rugger. Sandakan and H. M. S. Foxglove vs.: H. M. S. Carlisle. Sandakan and Foxglove won 17-3.

label: text
text: 14th, H. M. S. Foxglove vs: Sandakan Asiatics. Foxglove won 2-1.

label: text
text: It was also found possible to cater for those who preferred the pleasures of the chase in its various forms.

label: text
text: Mr. Rowe conducted a party to Dewhurst Bay on the 11th in the Berhala, returning the next day. Excellent sport was from all accounts obtained and the bag included a deer whose head was quite a decent one. A herd of tembadau was also encountered but was not depleted, though the fact of meeting with these animals,

label: paragraph_title
text: FLYING GOLFER.

label: text
text: 440 MILES TO PLAY A GAME FOR A WAGER

label: text
text:
Mr. R. Graham Murray, son of Lord Dunedin, one of the Lords of Appeal, makes most of his golfing expeditions by air.
He was referee of the golf match in which Sir E. Holderness and Mr. T. A. Torrance met Duncan and Mitchell at Sandy Lodge, Northwood, and in the afternoon his aeroplane was circling over the course ready for him to fly home.

label: text
text: Mr. Murray recently for a wager agreed to fly to Westward Hol Devon, about 220 miles, play two rounds of the championship course there, and be back in London in time for dinner the same evening. Starting at 9 a.m. he won the wager comfortably.

label: text
text: The flight to Westward's Ho! with a following wind took him 88 minutes.

text: which is by no means a certainty even in that locality, was regarded as most fortunate.

label: text
text:
By the kind invitation of Mr. Brower, the Manager, another party spent two days on Lode Estate, and though their bag was confined to one pig they returned none the less delighted with the experience.
On the 13th a fish-bombing expedition was organised, a steam launch being generously placed at the party's disposal for the afternoon. Messrs. Garry and S. W. Matthews accompanied the expeditious, which started tamely, the first 3 charges resulting merely in a catch of a number of "tiddlers" and fish like diminutive sardines. A move was then made towards Berhala, where a splendid haul was obtained, including a number of mullet and other fish, sufficient we were told to supply the whole ship's company of the Carlisle with three or more good sized fish apiece. The last charge drew blank except for the record-Sized fish of the afternoon, an enormous mullet which we understand was much enjoyed that evening.

label: text
text: The Carlisle left for Hongkong on the evening of the 14th and the Foxglove for the same port at daylight on the 15th. We can assure them that we shall look forward to their return and that they, in common with the rest of H.M. Ships that have visited us this year to our great delight, will be certain of the warmest of welcomes, and we trust that on the next occasion Lieut. Commander Acland, R.N., and Paymaster Lieut. Commander Pafford, R.N., will not be, as on this occasion, confined to a bed of sickness during most of their visit.

label: paragraph_title
text: GOLF

label: text
text: The method of selecting the English and Scottish teams for the international match has been for some time a subject of discussion.

label: text
text: Hitherto, the predominant power in this, as in other golfing affairs; has been vested in the Royal and Ancient Club, who now feel, however, that, owing to the work which devolves upon its committee, the task should be handed over to the national unions.

label: text
text: "Golf Illustrated" announces that a change is likely to take place in connection with this year's contest, due to be decided on the Royal North Devon links at Westward Ho! on Saturday, May 23. It is stated that the teams will be picked by the English and Scottish Unions respectively.

label: paragraph_title
text: CUP-FINAL MONEY.

label: text
text: The spectators at the Association Football Cup final between Sheffield United and Cardiff City at the Wembley Stadium is stated to have numbered about 90,000. The record attendance was in 1923, when 126,047 people paid £27,776 to see Bolton beat West Ham.

label: text
text: The Football Association takes one-third of the net receipts, the remainder being equally divided between the two clubs concerned in the match. The exhibition authorities receive an agreed sum for the use of the Stadium.

label: text
text: The Football Association's share in 1923 was £9,452, and last year, when the attendance was 91,675, £6,449.

label: paragraph_title
text: A PROMISING BATSMAN.

label: text
text:
Amongst the several armateurs who are expected to transfer their allegiance from one county to another this season is R. L. Holdsworth, late of Warwickshire, whose services Sussex hope to have for some of their matches. Educated at Repton and at Magdalen College, Oxford, Holdsworth was awarded his Blue in. 1913, and in the same year appeared with considerable success for Warwickshire. In his initial season of first-class cricket he scored 742 runs, with an average of 32.26, including a century for his 'Varsity against the M.C.C. at Lord's.
